# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-bacnet/server"
```

Package server is a BACnet/IP server: it serves one Device (package server/object) on one BACnet/IP endpoint.

One receive loop parses every frame. Confirmed and unconfirmed requests are executed by a bounded pool of workers; the receive loop itself only answers what needs no handler (Reject, Abort, repeated requests) and drives segmentation. COV and event notifications are sent by the server's own requester, with retries for confirmed ones.

The server is silent unless WithLogger or WithDiagnosticFunc is given, keeps no package-level state, and Close waits for every goroutine it started.

The application's code (Hooks, objects, the diagnostic function) runs on the server's goroutines. Code that does not return normally is stopped there, reported as a diagnostic with its stack, and the server goes on (see Hooks). Close may be called from such code.

type BBMD interface {
	// HandleBVLC processes one inbound BVLC message that is not a plain

### type Hooks

```go
type Hooks struct {
	// BeforeWrite is called before a WriteProperty, each write of a
	// WritePropertyMultiple, an AddListElement or RemoveListElement (the
	// Write then holds the elements as a constructed value), or an
	// AtomicWriteFile is applied, and before each write a Schedule makes to
	// the objects it references (that call comes from the housekeeping
	// goroutine, not from a worker, with the server's context). For
	// AtomicWriteFile the Write names File_Size and holds a constructed
	// value: the start position (Signed) followed by the data, one Octet
	// String for stream access or one per record for record access. A
	// returned error is sent as the answer (see object.Err). Default: allow.
	BeforeWrite func(ctx context.Context, obj bacnet.ObjectIdentifier, w object.Write) error
	// BeforeDelete is called before DeleteObject removes a deletable
	// object. Default: allow.
	BeforeDelete func(ctx context.Context, obj bacnet.ObjectIdentifier) error
	// Reinitialize is called for ReinitializeDevice after the password was
	// checked; the SimpleACK is sent when it returns nil. Default:
	// acknowledge COLDSTART, WARMSTART and ACTIVATE_CHANGES and do nothing,
	// and refuse START_BACKUP to ABORT_RESTORE with
	// services/service-request-denied (there is no backup procedure).
	Reinitialize func(ctx context.Context, state service.ReinitializedStateOfDevice) error
	// TimeSync is called for TimeSynchronization (utc false) and
	// UTCTimeSynchronization (utc true).
	//
	// The services below act only through their hook: without it they are
	// not listed in Protocol_Services_Supported, a confirmed request is
	// rejected with unrecognized-service and an unconfirmed one ignored.
	TimeSync func(t service.TimeSynchronization, utc bool)
	// PrivateTransfer handles Confirmed/UnconfirmedPrivateTransfer. For a
	// confirmed one the returned elements are the resultBlock.
	PrivateTransfer func(ctx context.Context, p service.PrivateTransfer, confirmed bool) ([]bacnet.Element, error)
	// TextMessage handles Confirmed/UnconfirmedTextMessage.
	TextMessage func(ctx context.Context, m service.TextMessage, confirmed bool) error
	// WriteGroup handles WriteGroup.
	WriteGroup func(ctx context.Context, w service.WriteGroup)
}
```

Hooks are the application's part in services that act on the device rather than on an object. Each runs on a worker with the request's deadline; a nil hook keeps the default given per field.

The contract of a hook, and of every other piece of the application's code that the server calls (API.md, "Hooks"):

  - Goroutine: a request worker, so several hooks run at the same time. BeforeWrite also runs on the housekeeping goroutine, for the writes a Schedule makes.
  - Blocking: a hook that waits holds its worker; with every worker held, requests wait in the queue and then get Abort out-of-resources. On the housekeeping goroutine it delays expiry, polling and event time delays. The context ends at the APDU timeout and at Close.
  - Calling back: a hook may call the Server, the Device and its objects.
  - Close: a hook may call Server.Close; Close then does not wait for the goroutine the hook runs on.
  - A hook that does not return normally is stopped at the server: a confirmed request is answered with Abort (other), a diagnostic of kind "callback" carries what the hook ended with and its stack, and the server goes on.

```go
type Option func(*config)
```

Option configures a Server.

#### func WithBBMD

```go

```

WithBBMD makes the server also act as a BBMD.

#### func WithCOVLimits

```go
func WithCOVLimits(maxSubscriptions int, maxLifetime time.Duration) Option
```

WithCOVLimits bounds COV subscriptions (default 256) and their lifetime (0: no limit, which also admits indefinite subscriptions).

#### func WithCOVReferenceLimit

```go
func WithCOVReferenceLimit(n int) Option
```

WithCOVReferenceLimit bounds the monitored references that all COV subscriptions hold together (default 4096): a SubscribeCOV counts two (Present\_Value and Status\_Flags), a SubscribeCOVProperty one or two, a SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple one per listed property. A subscription beyond it fails with resources/no-space-to-add-list-element, as one beyond WithCOVLimits does.

#### func WithDecodeLimits

```go
func WithDecodeLimits(l bacnet.DecodeLimits) Option
```

WithDecodeLimits sets the decode limits for inbound frames. The default is bacnet.DefaultDecodeLimits with MaxAPDUSize raised to MaxDatagramSize, so an APDU longer than Max\_APDU\_Length\_Accepted is still served; set MaxAPDUSize to drop such frames.

#### func WithDiagnosticFunc

```go
func WithDiagnosticFunc(fn func(Diagnostic)) Option
```

WithDiagnosticFunc receives every diagnostic. It runs on whichever goroutine of the server noticed the condition (the receive loop, a worker, housekeeping, a notification) and must not block. It may call Server.Close. A function that does not return normally is stopped by the server and reported to the logger of WithLogger, if there is one.

WithHooks installs application hooks.

WithSegmentation sets segmentation support: maxSegments (2..255; 0 disables segmentation) and the proposed window size (1..127).

#### func WithTransactionOptions

```go

```

WithTransactionOptions sets APDU timeout, retries and segment timeout for the server's own confirmed requests (notifications) and segmented replies; they are also the values of the Device's APDU properties.

#### func WithTransport

```go
func WithTransport(t bip.Transport) Option
```

WithTransport serves on t instead of opening a UDP socket. Close closes t.

#### func WithWorkers

```go
func WithWorkers(workers, queue int) Option
```

WithWorkers sets the number of request workers (default 4) and the number of requests that may wait for one (default 64). A confirmed request that finds the queue full is answered with Abort (out-of-resources); an unconfirmed one is dropped.

### type RecipientLimits

```go
type RecipientLimits struct {
	// PendingPerDestination bounds the server's confirmed requests that
	// wait for an answer from one destination (default 8). Beyond it a
	// confirmed COV notification waits its turn and a confirmed event
	// notification is dropped with an "event" diagnostic.
	PendingPerDestination int
	// Addresses bounds the device address cache (default 256): the event
	// recipients whose I-Am the server keeps, and the Who-Is requests for
	// unbound recipients that are outstanding at once. A full cache makes
	// room by dropping the entry heard from longest ago.
	Addresses int
	// Routes bounds the router table (default 64), and the networks a
	// router is being asked for at once. A full table makes room by
	// dropping the route used or heard from longest ago.
	Routes int
	// RouteRecheck is the shortest time between two
	// Who-Is-Router-To-Network the server sends for one network because
	// another node than the router that answered shows up for it (default
	// 5 minutes).
	RouteRecheck time.Duration
}
```

RecipientLimits bound what the server keeps and holds for the recipients of its notifications. A zero field keeps its default.

### type SegmentLimits

```go
type SegmentLimits struct {
	// Reassemblies bounds the segmented requests being reassembled at once
	// (default 64); ReassembliesPerOrigin bounds those from one B/IP node
	// (default 16), and ReassemblyOctets the octets they buffer together
	// (default 4 MiB). The first segment of a request beyond them is
	// answered with Abort out-of-resources.
	Reassemblies          int
	ReassembliesPerOrigin int
	ReassemblyOctets      int
	// Replies bounds the segmented replies being transmitted at once
	// (default 32), RepliesPerOrigin those to one B/IP node (default 8). A
	// request whose reply would exceed them is answered with Abort
	// out-of-resources.
	Replies          int
	RepliesPerOrigin int
}
```

SegmentLimits bound the server's segmented transactions as a whole. A zero field keeps its default.

#### func New

```go
func New(dev *object.Device, opts ...Option) (*Server, error)
```

New starts a server for dev. It opens a UDP socket unless WithTransport is given, and starts the receive loop and the workers.

#### func (Server) Close

```go
func (s *Server) Close() error
```

Close stops the server: it stops receiving, ends in-flight transactions and subscriptions, waits for every goroutine and closes the transport. Close is idempotent and safe to call from several goroutines; every call returns once the server is closed. After Close, IAm returns an error that matches bacnet.ErrClosed.

Close may be called from the application's code that the server runs: a hook, a method of an object, the diagnostic function, an observer. It then waits for every goroutine of the server but the one it was called on, and returns. That goroutine ends by itself when the code that called Close returns: the request it was serving is completed without an answer on the network (the transport is closed), and no further request, poll or event evaluation is started on it. Do not call Close from a Property Get or Set function: those run with the object's lock held, which the goroutines Close waits for may need.

#### func (Server) Device

```go
func (s *Server) Device() *object.Device
```

Device returns the served Device.

#### func (Server) IAm

```go
func (s *Server) IAm() error
```

IAm broadcasts an I-Am for the device (at start-up, for example). It is not sent while DeviceCommunicationControl disables initiation. After Close it returns an error that matches bacnet.ErrClosed (and context.Canceled, which it returned before v0.9.1).

```go
func (s *Server) Local() bip.Endpoint
```

Local returns the local BACnet/IP endpoint.
